title: Latency Shepherded Autotune with Tiered Failovers
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Our current cost-autotune recommendations (batching + KV caching) occasionally push aggressive configs that reduce token cost but create tail latency regressions for a small percentage of cohorts. We need an automated application path that actively shepherds optimization work by coupling per-cohort SLO awareness with multi-tiered failover behavior and anomaly detection.

Goal: Build an orchestration layer and runtime adapters that: 1) propose batching/caching profiles per traffic cohort, 2) apply them progressively with shadow probing and slow-roll soft-cuts, 3) enforce per-cohort latency/throughput limiters and SLO-aware routing, and 4) detect anomalies rapidly and execute staged rollback (soft revert -> full revoke) while preserving availability.

Scope: This ticket covers the design and implementation of the "Latency Shepherd" controller: policy language for limits, cohort tagging and routing hooks, anomaly detectors (statistical + signal-based), staged apply/rollback primitives, and dashboarding/alerts for on-call. It also includes integration points with Cost Recommendation engine and the Console rollout UI.

Key constraints: must not increase p99 by >5ms for high-SLA customers, must support canary sizes down to 0.1% traffic, and must be compatible with Dedicated and Private deployments where routing decisions may be constrained by network topology.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can apply a profile to a named cohort with staged traffic percentages (0.1%, 1%, 10%, 100%)
Per-cohort latency limiter supports absolute threshold and relative SLO budget checks before advancing rollout
Shadow probe pipeline runs 5% traffic by default and reports delta metrics (latency, error-rate, cost) to the rollout dashboard
Anomaly detector triggers automatic soft-cut (pause advancement) within 2 minutes of a 3-sigma deviation in p95 or a 30% increase in error-rate
Rollback workflow supports soft revert (traffic reweight to baseline) and full revoke (restore previous config) with audit trail and PR link
End-to-end unit/integration tests for controller logic with synthetic traces, and an e2e smoke test on staging that verifies canary and rollback behavior
rollout_plan: Initial internal dogfood on non-customer staging clusters targeting low-risk cohorts
Week 1: run in monitoring-only mode for 24/7 ingestion and alert tuning
Week 2: enable auto-apply at 0.1% canary for selected internal workloads
Week 3: expand to 1% then 10% after manual sign-off; enable auto-rollback rules
GA conditional on <5% incidents related to rollout and documented runbook updates
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy parser, limiter, and router decision logic
Load tests that simulate 5 distinct cohorts with varying seq lengths to validate batching behavior
Chaos tests that inject delayed KV cache responses and validate soft-cut triggers
Integration tests: cost-recommendation -> controller -> runtime config apply -> metrics ingestion
Manual canary exercise with synthetic prompts to validate SLO preservation and rollback timing
notes: 2026-02-19 - Kickoff: scoped with Product (Priya Nair) and Design; linked high-level PRD: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CO/Latency+Shepherd+PRD
2026-02-25 - Prototype: implemented limiter shim in staging runtime; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1129
2026-03-03 - Design review: agreed on two-tier rollback (soft-cut -> full revoke) and use of shadow probes for drift detection
2026-03-09 - Observability: added metrics to telemetry ingestion - shepherd.rollout.delta_p95, shepherd.rollout.cost_delta, shepherd.anomaly.score
2026-03-12 - Risk review: SRE flagged potential cross-cohort routing loops; added guard to ensure at most one active shepherded rollout per model-version per-region
monitoring_queries: runtime.batch.size distribution for shepherded cohorts vs baseline
estimated_savings: 15-30% average token-cost reduction for batched workloads after full rollout; expect diminishing returns for short prompt workloads
risk_assessment: Primary risks: (1) silent latency regressions for niche cohorts - mitigated by shadow probing and p95 delta alerts; (2) cascading rollbacks causing oscillations - mitigated by cooldown windows and single-active-rollout-per-model lock; (3) misclassification of cohorts leading to high CPU - mitigated by tuning cohort definitions and gradual canaries. Contingency: emergency feature-flag to disable all shepherd actions and fall back to baseline routing.
